items.stem: The NIST AI RMF is best described as:

options.text: Voluntary guidance for managing AI risks, not a certification
options.rationale: Correct: it is a framework, not a compliance certificate.

options.text: A legally binding regulation with fines
options.rationale: It is voluntary, not a law.

options.text: A certification you can pass or fail
options.rationale: There is no RMF pass/fail certificate.

items.explanation: Correct: it is a framework, not a compliance certificate.

items.stem: Which TWO are core functions of the NIST AI RMF? (Select TWO.)

options.rationale: Correct: Map is a core function (establishing context and risks).
Correct: Manage is a core function (acting on prioritised risks).
Not one of the named RMF functions.

items.explanation: Correct: Map is a core function (establishing context and risks).

items.stem: Why is the RMF presented as continuous rather than a one-off checklist?

options.text: AI risks change over time, so govern/map/measure/manage must be revisited
options.rationale: Correct: the functions are iterative across the lifecycle.

options.text: Because it must be done exactly once at launch
Because it certifies the system permanently

options.rationale: It includes, not replaces, ongoing measurement.
